questions.question: Technologies in use today have life span of decades
questions.explanation: Accepted answer as per the official NPTEL assignment evaluation.
questions.context:
Engineers and Scientists

We live in a world that is filled with a wide range of technologies that we use and we take for granted. The speed with which new technologies appear and disappear is constantly increasing. These days many of the gadgets we buy get outdated in a time frame of two to three years. This is a short time frame since many of the technologies in use are robust enough to physically last several years. However, in terms of features and utility, they get outdated much sooner than that. This is also a short time frame relative to how long technologies were used two or three decades ago. An example is the media used to store music. While gramophone records and cassettes lasted decades, DVDs have fast disappeared. Almost any mobile phone or computer purchased these days become obsolete in two to three years.

Behind this vast moving world of technologies, is a worldwide army of scientists and engineers. They are constantly on the prowl for making advances to existing technologies. Many industries, companies, and educational institutions are filled with scientists and engineers. While there may be some similarities in the tasks they are involved in, there are also some differences.

An engineer in an industry setting usually faces several technical trouble shooting challenges. Such challenges, with stiff timelines, require substantial familiarity with information databases, and characterization techniques, to be successfully addressed. Addressing trouble shooting challenges are often based on the selection and use of the best available resources and substitutes. The types of questions the engineer is faced with include questions of the sort:

1. Is there a lighter material readily available which can replace the existing material in the product?
2. Why is a specific batch of the product not as good as another batch?
3. Will it be possible for this product to function with lesser parts than it currently has?

Answers to such questions enable the industry meet the demands of their customers at lower costs and with greater reliability.

A scientist in a university or laboratory setting faces a different kind of challenge. The questions the scientist wishes to answer are:
1. Why is the value of any specific property of a material what it is?
2. What is the fundamental science behind the property?
3. What are the limits, if any, to this property?

Answers to such questions enable one to design new materials and to push the capabilities of existing materials.

Based on the professional setting a materials specialist ends up in, he/she will likely get pulled into one of the above types of activities. However, having both - a good feel for the fundamental sciences, as well as an understanding of the engineering approach to relate to the real world, can greatly enhance the value of a materials scientist/engineer to his or her organization.

At the same time, it usually takes considerable experience to fully understand, appreciate, and make use of the linkages between fundamental science and the world of engineering. Experience and systematic studies provide us with the insight to make the connections between the real-world inventions and the science behind them. Such insight helps us truly appreciate the contributions of the scientist as well as the engineer in shaping our interactions with the world around us. Such insight also enables us to take our technical pursuits to greater heights and wider reaches, and hence is desirable.

questions.question: Global warming is only a theoretical phenomenon
questions.explanation: Accepted answer as per the official NPTEL assignment evaluation.
questions.context:
Global warming refers to the idea that the temperature of the planet is, on average, increasing. It is a topic of considerable discussion and debate internationally because there are differing views on the severity of the phenomenon, the cause for the phenomenon, remedial measures to be considered and the financial impact of such remedial measures.

There is very strong experimental evidence that global warming is a real phenomenon. 10 of the hottest years recorded in history have all occurred in the last 15 years or so.

There is also strong reason to believe that the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere, directly impacts the raise in temperature observed globally. This evidence can be seen in the strong correlation between temperature and atmospherical carbon dioxide data collected in the past nearly 60 years, as well as in the temperature and carbon dioxide data that can be obtained for more than 100,000 years, from ice core samples obtained from Antarctica.

Based on energy usage patterns as well as the amount of carbon dioxide released as a function of the energy usage, it is possible to see how human activity can impact carbon dioxide content in the atmosphere in a significant manner. In fact a simple calculation will show that with the present level of energy usage, assuming all of it is from crude oil, the amount of carbon dioxide in the atmosphere will double in less than 100 years.

In addition to carbon dioxide, there are other gases as well that can accelerate global warming, some much more severely than carbon dioxide. However in terms of sheer quantity in the atmosphere, carbon dioxide is the most significant contributor to global warming.

The controversy over what needs to be done to combat global warming, is purely one of short term economic impact. Nations which release the most carbon dioxide total, as well the most carbon dioxide per-capita, are both reluctant to take measures to curb the release of carbon dioxide since it impacts quality of life of their populations in the short term. However there is grave danger in assuming such a short term outlook to this issue. If this issue is not addressed urgently, the planet may become unliveable in a relatively short time and at that point, with the very existence of humanity in question, it will look completely absurd to place a few comforts above survival of the planet.

Nature controls us indirectly by causing severe weather patterns that shut down cities for days and months. It is much more prudent that we address this issue on our initiative rather than wait for nature to complete the arguments in this context.

questions.question: GIS stands for _________.
questions.explanation: Self-explanatory/explained in lectures.

questions.question: ____________ analysis is descriptive and exploratory based on very large and complex data sets.
questions.explanation: Spatial analysis is descriptive and exploratory because GIS studies patterns, relationships, and trends using large spatial datasets such as maps, satellite imagery, and census information. It helps in understanding geographic phenomena and decision-making.

questions.question: Majority of GIS definitions focus on data, software, hardware, __________ and __________.
questions.explanation: Most GIS definitions include users and methods because GIS is not only about computers and software; it also depends on skilled people and systematic procedures for collecting, analysing, and interpreting spatial data.

questions.question: An excel sheet linked to map with village name, population, area, number of households etc. is an example of ___________.
questions.explanation: An Excel sheet linked with map information such as village name, population, area, and households is called attribute data because it provides descriptive information about geographic features stored in the map.

questions.question: Keyboard, monitor, cables, digitizers and scanners belong to ____________.
questions.explanation: Devices such as keyboards, monitors, scanners, digitizers, and cables are part of GIS hardware because they are the physical components required to input, process, display, and store GIS data.

questions.question: Postal code is an example of __________.
questions.explanation: A postal code represents a specific geographic location or area, therefore it is considered an example of spatial data. Spatial data describes the position or location of features on Earth.

questions.question: GIS was 1st introduced by ___________, who is also considered as father of GIS.
questions.explanation: Roger Tomlinson is known as the “Father of GIS” because he developed the first operational Geographic Information System, the Canada Geographic Information System (CGIS), in the 1960s.

questions.question: Direct coordinate entry is an example for ____________.
questions.explanation: Direct coordinate entry is a method of data input because geographic coordinates are entered directly into the GIS system to create or define spatial features.

questions.question: Web GIS consists of ______________ and ____________.
questions.explanation: Web GIS works through a combination of a server and client. The server stores and processes GIS data, while the client (web browser or application) allows users to access and visualize the information online.

questions.question: “Bhuvan” is the Indian Geo-platform to obtain
questions.explanation: Bhuvan, developed by Indian Space Research Organisation, provides multiple types of geospatial information including satellite imagery, rainfall data, and vector layers. Therefore, the correct answer is All of the above.

questions.question: Attribute data is managed and manipulated by _____________.
questions.explanation: Attribute data is managed using a DBMS (Database Management System) because DBMS organizes, stores, updates, and retrieves non-spatial information linked to geographic features in GIS.

questions.question: In a real-world model, the attributes are linked to _____________.
questions.explanation: In a real-world GIS model, attributes are linked to a database because databases store descriptive information (such as name, population, or land use) associated with spatial features shown on maps.

questions.question: Ranking of an attribute is given by _____________ scale.
questions.explanation: The ordinal scale is used for ranking attributes because it arranges data in a meaningful order or hierarchy, such as low, medium, and high, without specifying exact differences between them.

questions.question: An electrical power cable can be represented appropriately using ___________ graphical feature.
questions.explanation: An electrical power cable is best represented using a line feature because it has length and connectivity but negligible width when mapped in GIS.

questions.question: Terrain of a place is categorised as _____________ phenomena.
questions.explanation: Terrain is considered a continuous phenomenon because elevation and landforms change gradually over space rather than existing as separate isolated features.

questions.question: Which of the following activity in a GIS routine is tedious and expensive?
questions.explanation: Data collection is the most tedious and expensive activity in GIS because gathering accurate spatial and attribute data from surveys, satellites, GPS, or fieldwork requires significant time, effort, and resources.

questions.question: While dealing with a raster data, one of the key considerations is____________.
questions.explanation: In raster data, resolution is a key consideration because it determines the size of each pixel and the level of detail represented in the dataset. Higher resolution provides more detail but requires larger storage and processing capacity.

questions.question: Every sample has equal probability to be chosen in __________ sampling.
questions.explanation: In random sampling, every sample has an equal probability of being selected. This reduces bias and ensures fair representation of the population.

questions.question: Digitizing is a method adopted to generate ___________ data.
questions.explanation: Digitizing is mainly used to generate vector data by converting maps, drawings, or images into digital points, lines, and polygons within a GIS environment.

questions.question: Migration and housing data are examples of _________ data.
questions.explanation: Migration and housing information are examples of socio-economic data because they describe social and economic characteristics of a population.

questions.question: Dangles are _____________ errors that occur during vector data input.
questions.explanation: Dangles are digitizing errors that occur during vector data input when lines fail to connect properly, such as overshoots or undershoots in network mapping.

questions.question: Elevation map is an example of _____________ data.
questions.explanation: An elevation map is considered continuous data because elevation changes gradually across the Earth’s surface rather than existing as separate isolated values.

questions.question: ____________ describes the world as a space filled with discrete, identifiable units.
questions.explanation: The object model describes the world as being made up of discrete and identifiable entities such as roads, buildings, rivers, and parcels of land.

questions.question: In a vector model, ____________ are usually called as nodes.
questions.explanation: In a vector model, end points are called nodes because they define the start and end locations of line features and help establish spatial connectivity.

questions.question: The degree of agreement between several measurements of a quantity is denoted as_______________.
questions.explanation: Precision refers to the degree of agreement among repeated measurements of the same quantity. Higher precision means the measurements are very close to each other.

questions.question: Redundancy of data can be observed in _________ model.
questions.explanation: Data redundancy is common in the spaghetti model because spatial relationships are not stored efficiently, causing repeated storage of boundaries and coordinates.

questions.question: The disadvantage of quad tree model is/are __________.
questions.explanation: The quad-tree model may suffer from disadvantages such as increased processing time, large storage requirements, and complex alterations, therefore the correct answer is All of the above.

questions.question: _____________ describe the terrain surface including the above ground objects numerically in the form of x, y, and z coordinates.
questions.explanation: A Digital Surface Model (DSM) represents terrain surfaces along with above-ground features such as buildings, vegetation, and other objects using x, y, and z coordinates.

questions.question: Connectivity, area definition and contiguity are basic principles of ____________.
questions.explanation: Connectivity, area definition, and contiguity are the main principles of topology, which defines spatial relationships between geographic features in GIS.

questions.question: An imaginary line on the ground joining the points having the same elevation at a specific interval is known as __________.
questions.explanation: An imaginary line joining points of equal elevation is called an isoline (or contour line). It is commonly used in topographic maps to represent terrain elevation.

questions.question: A lake with its exact boundary can be marked using _______ model.
questions.explanation: A lake with an exact boundary is best represented using the vector model because vector polygons can accurately define precise boundaries and shapes of geographic features.

questions.question: 1mm on a map drawn at a scale of 1:50,000 represent _________ on the ground.
questions.explanation: A map scale of 1:50,000 means 1 unit on the map represents 50,000 of the same units on the ground. Therefore, 1 mm on the map = 50,000 mm = 50 m on the ground.

questions.question: How is a city most likely to be represented on a 1:25,000 scale map?
options: As a collection of points, lines and areas
answer: As a collection of points, lines and areas
questions.explanation: On a 1:25,000 large-scale map, a city is shown in greater detail using points, lines, and areas to represent roads, buildings, rivers, and boundaries.

questions.question: The _______ projection is an example of a cylindrical projection.
questions.explanation: The Mercator projection is a type of cylindrical projection because it projects the Earth’s surface onto a cylinder. It is widely used for navigation.

questions.question: The prime meridian runs through _________________.
questions.explanation: The Prime Meridian passes through Greenwich, England, and is defined as 0° longitude. It is the reference line for measuring east and west longitudes.

questions.question: A small-scale map would show
options: A larger geographic area than a large-scale map
A smaller geographic area than a large-scale map
The same geographic area as a large-scale map, just at a smaller resolution
answer: A larger geographic area than a large-scale map
questions.explanation: A small-scale map covers a larger geographic area but with less detail compared to a large-scale map. Examples include world or country maps.

questions.question: ___________ projection is accurate in the mid-latitude zone.
questions.explanation: Conic projections are most accurate in the mid-latitude regions because distortion is minimized along the standard parallels. They are commonly used for regional maps.

questions.question: Conformal maps could preserve __________ of a map property.
questions.explanation: Conformal maps preserve the shape of small areas and maintain local angles, although area and distance may become distorted.

questions.question: Actual area of Greenland is __________ than/to Africa, and this is due to Mercator distortion.
questions.explanation: Greenland appears much larger on the Mercator projection but in reality, its actual area is much smaller than Africa. This difference is caused by distortion near the poles.

questions.question: Which of the following represents positions as X, Y and Z coordinates (3D)?
questions.explanation: A geocentric coordinate system represents locations using X, Y, and Z coordinates in three-dimensional space, measured from the Earth’s centre.

questions.question: Georeferencing using mailing address is also known as __________.
questions.explanation: Assigning geographic coordinates using a mailing address is called geocoding. It converts addresses into spatial locations that can be mapped in GIS.

questions.question: __________ refers to how closely repeated measurements agree with each other.
questions.explanation: Precision measures the consistency of repeated measurements, regardless of whether they are close to the true value.

questions.question: Which factor can reduce the reliability of GIS spatial data?
questions.explanation: Reliability decreases when data is old, collected improperly, or has low spatial resolution.

questions.question: An error matrix in remote sensing is mainly used for evaluating __________.
questions.explanation: Error matrices compare classified images with reference data to assess classification accuracy.

questions.question: Producer’s accuracy in a confusion matrix is calculated using __________.
questions.explanation: Producer’s accuracy is the ratio of correctly classified pixels to the column total.

questions.question: Incorrect inclusion of pixels into a category is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Commission error occurs when pixels are wrongly assigned to a class where they do not belong.

questions.question: Which of the following represents a topology error in vector GIS?
questions.explanation: Overshoots occur when vector lines extend beyond their intended intersection points.

questions.question: Reducing the number of unnecessary vertices in a line feature is called __________.
questions.explanation: Line simplification reduces coordinate points while preserving the general shape of the feature.

questions.question: The alignment of two raster datasets into the same coordinate framework is called __________.
questions.explanation: Coregistration ensures multiple raster datasets spatially align correctly.

questions.question: Which transformation method stretches a map layer to fit predefined control points?
questions.explanation: Rubber sheeting adjusts spatial data geometrically to match reference control points.

questions.question: In digital image processing, the dominant wavelength or actual color is represented by __________.
questions.explanation: Hue defines the actual perceived color such as red, green, or blue.

questions.question: GPS determines the location of a receiver using the principle of __________.
questions.explanation: GPS works on the principle of trilateration, where distances from multiple satellites are used to determine the exact position of a receiver.

questions.question: The GPS space segment mainly consists of __________ satellites.
questions.explanation: The standard GPS constellation consists of 24 operational satellites orbiting the Earth.

questions.question: GPS signals are transmitted in the __________ region of the electromagnetic spectrum.
questions.explanation: GPS satellites transmit signals in the microwave region because microwaves can pass through clouds, rain, and fog with minimal interference.

questions.question: The Indian Regional Navigation Satellite System (IRNSS) consists of __________ satellites.
questions.explanation: IRNSS, also known as NavIC is made up of 7 satellites providing regional navigation services around India.

questions.question: Which GNSS system was developed by Russia?
questions.explanation: GLONASS is the satellite navigation system developed and operated by Russia.

questions.question: Errors in GPS signals caused due to reflection from nearby buildings are known as __________.
questions.explanation: Multipath errors occur when GPS signals bounce off buildings or other surfaces before reaching the receiver.

questions.question: The largest source of GPS positioning error is generally caused by __________.
questions.explanation: Charged particles in the ionosphere delay GPS signals, causing significant positioning errors.

questions.question: WAAS is mainly used to improve __________.
questions.explanation: WAAS (Wide Area Augmentation System) improves GPS navigation accuracy and reliability, especially for aviation purposes.

questions.question: The GPS master control station is located in __________.
questions.explanation: The GPS master control station responsible for monitoring and controlling GPS satellites is located at Colorado Springs, USA.

questions.question: Selective Availability (SA) in GPS was officially turned off in the year __________.
questions.explanation: Selective Availability, which intentionally reduced GPS accuracy for civilian users, was discontinued in 2000 to allow improved positioning accuracy.

questions.question: Raw facts and figures collected for processing are known as __________.
questions.explanation: Data refers to unprocessed facts and figures that can later be organized into meaningful information.

questions.question: Organized and meaningful data is called __________.
questions.explanation: When raw data is processed and arranged in a meaningful context, it becomes information.

questions.question: A collection of related data stored systematically in a computer system is known as __________.
questions.explanation: A database stores organized data in a structured manner for easy access and management.

questions.question: The full form of DBMS is __________.
questions.explanation: DBMS stands for Database Management System, which helps in storing, managing, and retrieving data efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a component of a database system?
questions.explanation: Key manager is not considered a standard component of a database management system.

questions.question: Which type of DBMS is most commonly used today?
questions.explanation: Relational DBMS (RDBMS) is the most widely used database model because it stores data in tables and supports efficient querying.

questions.question: A field that uniquely identifies each record in a table is called __________.
questions.explanation: A primary key uniquely identifies every record or tuple in a relational database table.

questions.question: In object-oriented databases, the process of hiding data and restricting direct access is called __________.
questions.explanation: Encapsulation protects object data by restricting direct access and allowing controlled interaction through methods.

questions.question: The process of organizing database tables to reduce redundancy is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Normalization reduces duplication and improves data integrity by organizing tables efficiently.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a relational database?
questions.explanation: MongoDB is a NoSQL document-oriented database, while the others are relational databases.

questions.question: In a database table, rows are called __________ and columns are called __________.
questions.explanation: In a database, each row represents a record, while each column represents a field or attribute.

questions.question: Which feature is mainly used to protect confidential database files?
questions.explanation: Encryption converts readable data into coded form to prevent unauthorized access.

questions.question: SQL was originally developed by __________.
questions.explanation: Structured Query Language (SQL) was initially developed by IBM for managing relational databases.

questions.question: The technique used to physically locate data on a disk efficiently is called __________.
questions.explanation: Hashing uses a hash function to quickly locate and retrieve stored data from disk storage.

questions.question: Storing geometric and attribute data in separate databases within GIS is known as __________.
questions.explanation: A hybrid GIS stores spatial and attribute information separately but links them together during analysis.

questions.question: Which of the following is a logical operator used in databases?
questions.explanation: AND is a logical operator used in database queries to combine conditions.

questions.question: Which among the following is a statistical operation?
questions.explanation: Maximum is a statistical operation used to determine the highest value within a dataset.

questions.question: The process of grouping attributes according to user-defined limits is called __________.
questions.explanation: Classification groups data into categories based on specified attribute ranges or rules.

questions.question: Which GIS feature ensures proper connection between vertices and edges during digitization?
questions.explanation: Snapping helps maintain topological consistency by connecting new features accurately to existing ones.

questions.question: Overlay analysis in GIS can be performed on __________.
questions.explanation: Overlay operations combine multiple spatial datasets and can be applied to both raster and vector formats.

questions.question: Which of the following is a logical operation instead of an arithmetic operation?
questions.explanation: Equal to is a logical comparison operator, while addition, subtraction, and multiplication are arithmetic operations.

questions.question: The result of a buffer operation in GIS is generally a __________ feature.
questions.explanation: Buffering creates polygon zones around spatial features at a specified distance.

questions.question: Network analysis in GIS mainly depends on __________.
questions.explanation: Network analysis requires connected paths, movement rules, and measurement definitions for routing and accessibility analysis.

questions.question: Bilinear interpolation uses the nearest __________ neighboring pixels.
questions.explanation: Bilinear interpolation calculates new pixel values using the 4 nearest neighboring pixels.

questions.question: Bicubic interpolation calculates output values using __________ neighboring pixels.
questions.explanation: Bicubic interpolation considers the nearest 16 pixels to produce smoother image resampling results.

questions.question: A GIS model representing terrain as continuous non-overlapping triangles is called __________.
questions.explanation: TIN (Triangulated Irregular Network) represents surfaces using connected triangular facets.

questions.question: A line joining locations of equal elevation on a map is known as a __________.
questions.explanation: Contour lines connect points having the same elevation above mean sea level.

questions.question: The rate of elevation change over a surface is called __________.
questions.explanation: Slope measures the steepness or rate of change in elevation between locations.

questions.question: Overlay analysis in GIS can be applied on __________.
questions.explanation: Overlay operations combine multiple spatial layers and can be performed on both raster and vector datasets.

questions.question: In remote sensing, sensors that emit their own energy to capture data are called __________ sensors.
questions.explanation: Active remote sensing systems, such as radar, transmit their own energy and record the reflected signal from Earth’s surface.

questions.question: Minimum number of control points required for georeferencing in QGIS is __________.
questions.explanation: At least three control points are required to accurately transform and align a raster image with real-world coordinates.

questions.question: QGIS can be used to create which type of spatial features?
questions.explanation: QGIS supports the creation and editing of all major vector feature types including points, lines, and polygons.

questions.question: The process of assigning real-world coordinates to a raster image is known as __________.
questions.explanation: Georeferencing links image pixels to actual geographic coordinates using control points.

questions.question: CRS in GIS stands for __________.
questions.explanation: CRS defines how spatial data is projected and represented on the Earth’s surface.

questions.question: Which statement about QGIS is correct?
questions.explanation: QGIS is a free and open-source GIS platform that works on multiple operating systems.

questions.question: Which option in QGIS is used to install additional tools and functionalities?
questions.explanation: Plugins allow users to extend QGIS capabilities with additional analysis and visualization tools.

questions.question: Which file format is most commonly used for raster datasets in GIS?
questions.explanation: GeoTIFF stores raster images along with geographic referencing information.

questions.question: A toposheet with scale 1:25,000 contains __________ detail compared to a 1:50,000 map.
questions.explanation: Larger-scale maps such as 1:25,000 show more detailed geographic information than smaller-scale maps.

questions.question: In QGIS field calculator, area values are converted from square meters to hectares by dividing by __________.
questions.explanation: One hectare equals 10,000 square meters, so area values are divided by 10,000.

questions.question: OpenStreetMap plugin in QGIS is mainly used for __________.
options: Base map and spatial data download
answer: Base map and spatial data download
questions.explanation: OpenStreetMap plugin provides base maps and allows downloading spatial information for GIS analysis.

questions.question: Which command is used to load a package in R?
questions.explanation: The library () function is used in R to load installed packages into the current session.

questions.question: Which function is used to create a dataframe in R?
questions.explanation: data.frame() is the standard function in R for creating tabular datasets.

questions.question: Which function is commonly used to display False Colour Composite (FCC) images in R?
questions.explanation: plotRGB() is used for plotting multi-band raster images as FCC or true-color composites.

questions.question: The cellStats() function in R is mainly used to calculate __________.
questions.explanation: cellStats() computes raster statistics such as minimum, maximum, mean, and standard deviation.

questions.question: Data created in Google Earth can be imported into QGIS using which format?
questions.explanation: KML is the standard format used for transferring spatial data from Google Earth into GIS software.

questions.question: Which dataset is freely available in the Indian Space Research Organisation Bhuvan Geoportal?
questions.explanation: LISS III satellite imagery is freely accessible through the Bhuvan Geoportal.

questions.question: Which interpolation method uses 16 neighboring pixels?
questions.explanation: Bicubic interpolation uses the nearest 16 pixels to create smoother resampled images.

questions.question: The process of assigning real-world coordinates to a raster image is called __________.
questions.explanation: Georeferencing links raster images with actual geographic coordinates on Earth.

questions.question: Which GIS operation creates zones around spatial features?
questions.explanation: Buffering creates polygon zones at specified distances around spatial features.

questions.question: Which GIS software is free and open-source?
questions.explanation: QGIS is an open-source GIS software used for mapping and spatial analysis.
